extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and academics acting as peer reviewers for PLOS journals (and journal peer reviewers generally)
extracted.subtask_description: Ethical guidance for researchers serving as peer reviewers, covering when to accept assignments, impartiality, conflicts of interest, confidentiality, professionalism, and compliance with COPE and journal policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support research integrity in peer review and publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: As a reviewer, you have a crucial role in supporting research integrity in the peer review and publishing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching purpose of reviewer conduct; reviewers should follow the basic ethical principles outlined on the page to promote transparency and integrity in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by COPE guidance and PLOS ethical policies
rubrics_metrics.description: These recommendations are based on the Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE) Ethical Guidelines for Peer Reviewers. PLOS is a member of COPE, abides by the COPE Core Practices and follows COPE’s best practice guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are expected to follow COPE guidance and PLOS policy on ethical publishing practice; links to COPE Core Practices and PLOS policy are provided for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose assignments wisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree to review a manuscript only if you have the appropriate subject expertise and a sufficient amount of time to complete the review, in accordance with the journal deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept reviews outside your expertise or when you cannot meet the deadline; assess both topical competence and availability before agreeing to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an objective, honest, and unbiased review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be objective, truthful, and free from bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep evaluation focused on the work's scientific/technical merits rather than personal views; follow the subsequent specific rules (declare conflicts, avoid bias based on authors' characteristics, do not impersonate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare any potentially competing interests and/or recuse yourself
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare any potentially competing interests and recuse themselves from assignments if they have a conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a conflict exists (financial, personal, professional, or other) that could bias the review, notify the editor and decline or be recused rather than proceeding with the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bias based on authors' origins or personal characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your perspective is not influenced by authors’ origins, nationality, beliefs, gender, or other characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess manuscripts on their merits only; do not allow unconscious or conscious prejudices about author identity or affiliations to affect your judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not impersonate another individual when reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not impersonate another individual in your work as a reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always perform reviews under your own identity and credentials; do not submit reviews under someone else's name or claim false authorship/identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor the confidentiality of the review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not share information about manuscripts or reviews during or after peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep draft manuscripts, review comments, and related communications confidential; do not disseminate data or ideas seen in a manuscript, nor discuss the manuscript with others without permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use information from the review process for personal advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use any information from the review process for your own advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never exploit privileged knowledge obtained through peer review (e.g., to advance your own research, solicit collaborations, or for financial gain).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be respectful and professional in review comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your review comments are professional. Keep your focus on the work and not on the individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame criticisms constructively, avoid ad hominem remarks, derogatory language, or unprofessional tone; focus on how the manuscript can be improved rather than attacking authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult additional reviewer role resources when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Further guidance on reviewer roles and responsibilities is available from organisations such as the Council of Science Editors and the International Committee of Medical Journal Editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt about specific responsibilities or best practices, consult these external resources (CSE Reviewer Roles and Responsibilities; ICMJE Responsibilities in the Submission and Peer Review Process) as supplemental guidance.
